description: Create an order — a request for items or material (any member can order; order managers fulfill). Put what you need into `lines`, one entry per thing, each with an optional `quantity`: "Bestell 5 Packungen Kopierpapier" is one line { description: "Packungen Kopierpapier", quantity: 5 }, a specific inventory item goes in as { itemId, quantity } instead (find ids with search_items), "any two of this drill model" as { modelId, quantity: 2 } (search_items rows carry the modelId), and "any five from this category" as { categoryId, quantity: 5 } (category ids from get_item_requirements) — for a model or category the store picks the concrete items, and ordering one with nothing free is allowed. `request` is the free-text framing around it ("für das Schulzimmer 201"), and at least one of request / lines / itemIds must be there. `neededBy` is when your user needs it — YOU resolve "bis Dienstag" to a calendar day and pass it as "2026-08-11". Only you know your user's timezone: this server has none and does no conversion, so a bare day is the safe form, and a full timestamp is accepted only WITH an explicit offset ("2026-08-11T00:00:00+02:00"). The legacy `neededByAt` epoch still works for older clients — pass exactly one of the two. The result echoes back `neededByAtIso`, the day that actually landed, so read it out to confirm the arithmetic was yours and it was right. `deliverToResourceId` is the person or location the items should go to (find ids with search_resources); omit it to deliver to yourself. Tell your user about the new order with its `webUrl` link — `orderId` is a machine handle for your follow-up calls, not something to read aloud. Recommended: pass a fresh `clientRequestId` (e.g. a UUID) with every new order — retrying with the SAME id returns the existing order instead of creating a duplicate.

clientRequestId.description: Optional but recommended: a unique id you generate for this request (e.g. a UUID). If the call times out or you retry, pass the SAME id — you'll get the existing order back instead of creating a duplicate. Use a fresh id for each new order.

deliverToResourceId.description: Person or location resource id to deliver to; defaults to you

itemIds.description: Shorthand for quantity-less inventory item lines; equivalent to lines: [{ itemId }]. Prefer `lines` when a quantity matters

lines.description: The requested lines, one entry per thing you need — each a specific inventory item, any instance of a model, any item of a category, or free text, each with an optional quantity

categoryId.description: Any item of this category, subcategories included, the store picks which (a category id from get_item_requirements) — e.g. "5 Stichsägeblätter"

description.description: Free text for something that is not in the inventory, e.g. "Packungen Kopierpapier"

itemId.description: This one inventory item (an id from search_items) — exactly one of itemId / modelId / categoryId / description per line

modelId.description: Any instance of this model, the store picks which (the modelId of a search_items row) — e.g. "2 Akku-Bohrschrauber" when it does not matter which two

quantity.description: How many (a whole number ≥ 1). Meaningful for material and stock, not for one serialized machine — leave it off there

neededBy.description: When the requester needs it, as a calendar day: "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g. "2026-08-11"). THIS is the form to use — a bare day has no timezone to get wrong. Your user says "bis Dienstag"; only YOU know which calendar day that is and which timezone they are in, because this server has no timezone and does no conversion. A full timestamp is accepted only WITH an explicit offset ("2026-08-11T00:00:00+02:00"), whose calendar day is then taken as seen in that offset; an offset-less timestamp is refused rather than guessed. Passing both neededByAt and neededBy is an error

neededByAt.description: When the requester needs it, as epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight of that day. Prefer `neededBy` — pass exactly one of the two

request.description: Free-text description of what you need (at least one of request/lines/itemIds is required)

name: create_order

neededByAt.description: The needed-by date that actually landed, epoch milliseconds. Absent when none was passed

neededByAtIso.description: The same date as a plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD" — read THIS back to your user, the date was YOUR arithmetic. A DAY, not a moment: the server does no timezone conversion

webUrl.description: Link to the new order in the web app — give your user THIS, never the raw `orderId` (that is a machine handle for your next call)

title: Create order
